source.title: Understanding the learned look-ahead behavior of chess neural networks

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. The implementation section says the paper's code link was omitted for review.
record.tranche_reason: It extends the prior Leela chess look-ahead analysis using activation patching and probing, and reports results for longer move sequences and alternative branches.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own probing, activation-patching, and head-ablation results. Numbers shown only in plots are recorded as figure only. Citations to other studies are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: It extends Jenner et al.'s Leela chess look-ahead analysis to 5th and 7th moves and alternative branches, using its own patching, probing and ablation results. Chess look-ahead is a new setting relative to the originals (LM rhyme planning, Future Lens, Wu et al.), so T3 rather than T1. Its results bear on V5 (look-ahead in chess) and on V6's horizon and heuristic questions.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude Leela processes information up to seven moves ahead, weaker for more distant moves, and highly dependent on puzzle pattern and checkmate. Some future moves go through shared, timing-insensitive head mechanisms such as L12H12, and the model considers multiple move sequences. They concede they cannot tell true planning from sophisticated pattern matching, yet argue the results challenge views of networks as mere statistical pattern matchers.
record.recipe_differences: Builds on Jenner et al.'s Leela analysis and uses related activation patching, probing, and ablation approaches, extending the analysis to longer sequences and alternative branches.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with puzzle-set move-square pattern, sequence length, and whether the position leads to checkmate. The seventh-move effects are weaker than nearer-move effects.
record.code_released: not stated; the paper's implementation link is omitted for review
record.problems: The authors say they cannot determine whether the behavior is true planning or sophisticated pattern matching; patching may miss distributed effects; the analysis is specific to chess; dataset constraints limited coverage of move patterns, especially for longer sequences; and the alternative-move analysis has a limited sample due to strict selection criteria.
record.rows_left_out: Not all plotted puzzle-set and attention-head results are itemized. The selected rows retain the stated seventh-move, contrasting fifth-move, and alternative-branch findings; additional conditions appear in Appendices B, D, E, and F.

untested.parts: Look-ahead in language-model multi-step reasoning and in Sokoban or other architectures; only one chess policy network is studied.
Whether the look-ahead is a plan or heuristic pattern matching; the authors say they cannot determine this.
All of it: rhyme planning in a frontier LM.
All of it: future-token decodability in language-model hidden states.
All of it: whether features are computed for later use rather than as a side effect.
All of it: rhyme planning in open-weight LMs.

missing.what: 3rd-move patching for 3-move sets (ordering 122 < 123 < 112), reproducing Jenner et al., and the ACC < ABC < AAC ordering across moves 3, 5 and 7
Probing for set 12345: 3rd and 5th moves and opponent moves decodable with high accuracy, peaking at layer 13; the 4th move is harder than the 5th
A distinct 2nd or 4th move square shows no significant direct patching role in any set
Checkmate dependence: L12H12 matters more in checkmate sets, L12H17 in non-checkmate sets
Attention-head patching peak log odds reduction of 0.73 for L12H12 in set 112

record.verdict_notes: The record's T1 is changed to T3: none of the original sources study chess. Most rows are figure-only, with values described qualitatively. The study is not an original source for any version. It is single-author, and its peer-review status is unclear: the preprint says 'under review' while the record says TMLR.

versions.untested_parts: Rhyming verse, candidate rhyme words, and interventions on rhyme words.
The study probes chess move-square information, not tokens several positions ahead in language-model hidden states.
It does not test whether features are computed for the purpose of helping later positions rather than as a side effect of next-step prediction.
No rhyme-planning test in smaller open-weight language models.
Tests look-ahead in chess only; it does not test multi-step reasoning in language models or Sokoban.
It examines context dependence and diminishing evidence at longer chess horizons, but does not establish whether the mechanism is a local heuristic or a general planning algorithm.

tranche.reason: Reports its own results on look-ahead in a chess policy transformer, extending earlier chess analysis to longer horizons and alternative branches.

source_check.notes: Row states describe the observed look-ahead effects relative to V5; chess-move horizons cannot be converted into language-model token horizons. The supplied preprint leaves true planning versus sophisticated pattern matching unresolved.

statements.correction: 15-layer Leela policy transformer; approximately 109 million parameters; current-board-only finetuned model from Jenner et al.; strong fifth-move patching in 11223; L12H12 fifth-to-first and fifth-to-third effects in 11223; alternative-third-square patching often improves the main move's odds; supplied version: arXiv v1, preprint under review.
statements.problem: The mechanistic findings and stated architecture size are supported. The supplied text does not identify the checkpoint as T82-768x15x24h or establish TMLR publication; it identifies itself as a preprint under review.

statements.correction: Set 11223: L12H12 fifth-to-first and fifth-to-third effects. Set 11234: fifth-to-first effect. Set 12223: fifth-to-third effect. Figures 17–18: zero ablation. Seventh-move effects are small; set 11233 retains third-to-first information transfer. Authors cannot distinguish true planning from sophisticated pattern matching.
statements.problem: The fifth-to-third path is incorrectly attributed to set 11234. Causal dependence on future-move information does not establish that shallow or heuristic explanations are absent.

statements.correction: Causal effects of fifth-move destination-square information on the current move; weaker seventh-move effects; strong puzzle-pattern dependence; true planning versus sophisticated pattern matching unresolved.
statements.problem: Describing the chess results as deep causal plans overstates what the interventions establish and omits the authors' unresolved planning-versus-pattern-matching distinction.
